payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish that the source mug itself has been moved to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass only when the combined visual evidence establishes both correspondence to the source mug and its position to the right of the edited headphones. Compare both edited mug candidates using body proportions, rim and interior, handle geometry, relative scale and appearance, accounting for changes in framing and possible rotation. Generic mug shape, similar taper or presence on the right is insufficient when those cues do not distinguish the right-hand candidate from the left-hand candidate. Consider evidence supporting and contradicting each correspondence; do not dismiss differences in interior, handle or appearance without weighing them together with the supporting cues. Exact color, scale and handle orientation preservation are not separate requirements. Fail when the evidence establishes that the source mug remains left of the headphones or otherwise has not reached the requested right-side position. Use unknown when the source mug's correspondence or resulting position remains unresolved. A blurred patch alone establishes neither retained identity nor successful removal, and lack of proof of completion is not proof of failure.
node.binding: Target: the light-blue mug with a left-facing handle in the source image. Reference: the headphones in each image. Compare the source mug with both edited candidates: the pale mug left of the headphones and the dark-interior mug right of the headphones. Inspect the far-left blue blurred patch only as ambiguous possible residual evidence, not as an identified mug. Assess whether the full cue combination distinguishes the right-hand candidate as the relocated source mug rather than a separate mug; if neither candidate can be identified reliably, return unknown. Compare object-relative placement with the edited headphones, allowing for changed framing, scale and headphone arrangement rather than relying on raw pixel coordinates.

node_traces.evidence: The source mug is light blue, relatively broad, with a left-facing handle and a dark blue interior. In the edited image, the pale mug left of the headphones has a right-facing handle and light interior, while the dark-interior mug to the right has a right-facing handle and appears smaller and more tapered. The right-hand candidate's dark interior is a supporting cue, but its appearance, proportions, scale, and handle orientation differ; the left candidate also differs in color, interior, and handle orientation. The far-left blue blur is ambiguous and does not establish identity. The visual evidence does not reliably distinguish which edited mug, if either, is the source mug, so its resulting position is unresolved.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is already specific; the unresolved result is not a schema, transport, or dependency failure (the check ran validly with no dependencies). Improve the decision criterion’s evidence integration rather than forcing the reference label: compare the source mug’s broad body and dark-blue interior with both edited candidates, and weigh the right candidate’s dark interior as a meaningful identity cue alongside its smaller/tapered body and right-facing handle. The pale left candidate’s light interior and different appearance also count against it. Do not treat changed scale, color, or handle orientation as automatic disproof, since these are not required invariants; likewise, do not infer identity from right-side placement alone. The far-left blur remains ambiguous and cannot establish either a retained mug or successful removal. The trace’s high confidence despite unresolved correspondence is a calibration signal: make confidence reflect the strength and conflict of the combined cues, and distinguish uncertainty about identity from evidence that some requested movement may have progressed. Keep unknown when correspondence truly cannot be resolved; do not convert the aggregate ‘partial’ label into atomic ground truth or lower the pass/fail standard merely to match it."}
